items.author: majq92
items.summary: Enables encoder layers in multimodal models to replicate when tensor-parallel size doesn't evenly divide attention heads or MLP intermediate dimensions.
items.body:
## Overview

Several multimodal encoders shard their attention by head count and their MLP by
intermediate size. When the tensor-parallel size does not divide those
dimensions, the sharding layers raise while the model is being constructed, so
the model cannot be loaded at all:

```
AssertionError: 20 is not divisible by 8
```

`ensure_divisibility` (`vllm/distributed/utils.py`) asserts, and
`QKVParallelLinear.__init__` calls it before any weight is allocated.

| `glmasr.py` | audio | 20 | 3, 6, 8, 16 |
| `glm4v.py` | vision |

items.title: [RFC]: Fault-tolerant sharded RDT weight sync: continue on surviving inference engines
items.author: hao-aaron
items.summary: RFC proposing fault-tolerant sharded RDT weight sync that continues on surviving inference engines instead of failing the entire round when one engine crashes or loses an RPC.
items.body:
### Motivation.

With the sharded RDT weight-transfer backend (as redesigned on the load plan in #68038, part of #64418), one failed inference engine fails the weight sync for every engine. An engine crash fails the round within seconds. A lost RPC fails it only after the 300 s HTTP timeout or stall watchdog. RL rollout pools run on preemptible or shared capacity and see both kinds of failure. The sync should continue on the engines that are still healthy and let the failed ones rejoin later.

This RFC lists the failure classes to handle, describes what happens today, and proposes a protocol.
discussion: Opened here by mistake; this is being drafted at https://github.com/hao-aaron/vllm/issues/23 for now.

## What

The NVLS AllGather-V and ReduceScatter-V kernels, and the ordered ReduceScatter-V used by batch-invariant mode, returned before their barrier when a CTA's `pid >= ep_max_tokens`. With this change every CTA enters the barrier. CTAs without rows only skip the copy loop, which is already bounded by `local_tokens`.

## Why

This is a robustness change, not a fix for an observed bug.

items.summary: On MI355X, MoRIIO PD serving can fail at the first requests with while VRAM is free: amdgpu counts VRAM that a NIC pins twice in the KFD allocation limit. This PR adds an opt-in to.
items.body:
## Overview

On MI355X, MoRIIO PD serving can fail at the first requests with `HIP error 209` while VRAM is free: amdgpu counts `hipMalloc` VRAM that a NIC pins twice in the KFD allocation limit ([ROCm/mori#721](https://github.com/ROCm/mori/issues/721)). This PR adds an opt-in `"custom_mem_pool": "AMD_GEM"` to `MoRIIOConnector`. items.author: zyulai
items.summary: In (upstream main ): This makes PCP and multi-LoRA serving mutually exclusive. Those are exactly the two features that are most useful together: PCP is for long-context prefill, and LoRA is for serving many tenants from one base model.
items.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

MRV2 prefill context parallelism (PCP, #46570) currently rejects LoRA at startup. In `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/pcp_manager.py:175` (upstream main `898a7c68c2`):

```python
if vllm_config.lora_config is not None:
    raise NotImplementedError("MRV2 PCP does not support LoRA yet.")
```

This makes PCP and multi-LoRA serving mutually exclusive. Those are exactly the two features that are most useful together: PCP is for long-context prefill, and LoRA is for serving many tenants from one base model. A user who needs both currently has to pick one.

I would like t
discussion: We will consider LoRA when enable PCP, and I think attention-only LoRA isn't enough

amdgpu-dkms counts `hipMalloc` memory that a NIC pins twice in the KFD allocation limit:

## Motivation

NPU Prefill query sharding can retain rank-local indexer Top-K rows, while MTP IndexShare exports its seed using full-batch last-query indices. items.body:
## Motivation

Zigzag prefill CP still declines the breakable prefill CUDA graph under pipeline parallelism through a `pp_size == 1` check in `ZigzagCPBCGInput.supports()`. That check predates the generic PP-stage support for prefill CP graphs (#48712): later stages now shard only positions and take the previous stage's CP-local PP proxy, stale proxy rows beyond the eager shard are zeroed, and middle stages send the eager per-rank row count so the next stage can replay or run eagerly on the same shard. Nothing in that path is interleave-specific, so zigzag can use it as is. Supersedes #47604.

items.author: ChengYao-amd
items.summary: Fixes missing KV connector offering of coarse-aligned prompt-end Mamba checkpoints, causing offloaded prefixes to lose Mamba state during reuse.

## Overview

When prefix-cache hits align to a unit coarser than the Mamba block, the prompt-end Mamba checkpoint is keyed for local hits but never offered to a KV connector, unless a prefill chunk happens to end exactly on it. items.author: kpham-sgl
items.summary: The unified-cache external linker looks up only the pages past the device-cache hit: builds its store lookup from, which starts at. A prefix that a rank keeps serving from its device cache therefore never touches the store, and the store's leases on that prefi…
items.body:
## Motivation

The unified-cache external linker looks up only the pages past the device-cache hit: `match()` builds its store lookup from `tail_hashes`, which starts at `device_hit_len`. A prefix that a rank keeps serving from its device cache therefore never touches the store, and the store's leases on that prefix lapse while the conversation is still active.

items.title: [Fix] dspark: Prevent Philox rounding from selecting a masked token
items.author: wuyii8941
items.summary: With logits and temperature 1, DSpark's Markov sampler can return token 0. Both the Torch and Triton implementations do this with the draft key for server seed 0, row 0, step 0 and counter 4,757,896.
items.body:
## Motivation

With logits `[-inf, 0]` and temperature 1, DSpark's Markov sampler can return token 0. Both the Torch and Triton implementations do this with the draft key for server seed 0, row 0, step 0 and counter 4,757,896. Token 1 draws the Philox word `0xffffff9f`. Converting that word to FP32 rounds it to 2³², so the uniform becomes exactly 1. Its exponential noise is infinite and its score ties the masked token at `-inf`.

The sharded verifier uses the same transform for its bonus draw. At counter 1,781,785 it accepts the sole supported draft token and then returns the masked token as i

items.title: [HiSparse] Reuse finished requests' GPU copies before cached prefixes
items.author: MatthewBonanni
items.summary: When a request finishes, HiSparse keeps its clean resident pages in the GPU pool as copies. They go to the free-queue tail, at the same LRU priority as prefix-cached indexer blocks.
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #68725.

When a request finishes, HiSparse keeps its clean resident pages in the GPU pool as copies. They go to the free-queue tail, at the same LRU priority as prefix-cached indexer blocks. That ordering is the bug:

- A host prefix hit needs the GPU indexer blocks; a copy only speeds up a hit that also finds them.
- A long request leaves about 1 indexer block and several resident copies per page.
- Later requests' copies therefore outlive earlier prefixes' indexer blocks, and re-sent prompts miss far below host-pool capacity.

### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8766.

In V1 trainers (`sync` and `colocate_async`), `_compute_advantage()` whitens advantages once over the full sampled batch, whereas `TrainingWorker.train_mini_batch()` splits the batch into `ppo_mini_batch_size` optimizer chunks without re-normalizing per chunk. When the sampled batch is larger than `ppo_mini_batch_size`, individual optimizer chunks can have non-zero token-weighted advantage means, introducing chunk-level policy-gradient drift.

This PR re-normalizes `mini_batch_td["advantages"]` per optimizer chunk in `TrainingWorker.train_mini_batch()`

## Summary

items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The fused `topkGating` kernel behind `topk_softmax` / `topk_sigmoid` only exists for specific expert counts:
- powers of two up to 128;
- 192, 256, 320, 384, 448, 512 and 576;
- 352, for sigmoid only.

Every other count, and every row-padded input, falls back to two unfused kernels, `moeSoftmax` + `moeTopK`, which are 3–7x slower. Expert-pruned checkpoints almost always land on such a count. This PR runs a fused kernel for any expert count up to 512. Counts that already had a fused kernel compile to exactly main's code.

## Claims

**Bad case fixed.*

items.body:
## Motivation

Each Mooncake prefill rank shards rooms over `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_QUEUE_SIZE` queues (default 4), one transfer worker thread each, keyed by the sum of the decode session ports. When sending one chunk raised, `transfer_worker` failed that room and then raised `Transfer thread failed ... is dead`, and the thread exited. Nothing drains that queue afterwards. Every later request hashed onto it waits out the waiting timeout (300 s) and aborts. Meanwhile the other queues keep producing output, so `/health_generate` keeps returning 200 and nothing restarts the server.

items.title: [HiSparse] Offload the indexer by default and split host_pool_gib with it
items.author: MatthewBonanni
items.summary: Before, cached prefixes were lost after a few prompts of other traffic, however large was. A prefix hit needs the indexer cache too, and that cache only lived on the GPU, where it was evicted quickly.
items.body:
Related to #68725.

## What changes

When HiSparse runs with prefix caching (the default), vLLM now also offloads the indexer cache to CPU. Before, cached prefixes were lost after a few prompts of other traffic, however large `host_pool_gib` was. A prefix hit needs the indexer cache too, and that cache only lived on the GPU, where it was evicted quickly ([root cause](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/68725#issuecomment-7013589195)).

Host memory use stays at what you configured: `host_pool_gib` is now the **total**, shared by the HiSparse pool and the indexer cache.

items.title: [Model][PERF] HY4 Flash Improvement
items.author: jeejeelee
items.summary: Optimizes HY4 Flash decoding by fusing norms, MoE all-reduce, and MLA sigmoid gates with breakable CUDA graphs for end-to-end performance gains.
items.body:
- Run HY4 Flash with breakable CUDA graphs so RMSNorm uses the vllm_c op
- Port the iHC boundary op and carry the MLP post across layers (HY4 + Flash)
- Fuse post-projection / MoE norms with the TP all-reduce; single MoE AR
- Fuse the gated MLA sigmoid gate with fused_sigmoid_gate_mul
- Fuse the Engram lookup norm and gated update; one projection GEMM and AR

EAGLE-3 checkpoints converted from the reference implementation store the aux layer ids nested as `eagle_config['eagle_aux_hidden_state_layer_ids']`. `get_eagle3_aux_layers_from_config()` only checked a drafter-style nested key (`layer_ids`) and the top-level attribute, so such checkpoints silently fell back to the model's default aux layers `(2, L//2, L-3)` with an INFO-level log only. A draft head trained on the checkpoint's declared ids then receives features captured from the wrong layers, and speculative decoding fails with no warning.

items.title: [ROCm][DSA] DCP global-key indexer prefill (opt-in)
items.author: andyluo7
items.summary: Opt-in ROCm prefill path for DSA indexers under decode-context parallelism. The base ROCm DCP prefill (#65685) scores each rank's key shard and merges the per-rank top-k candidates.
items.body:
## Overview

Opt-in ROCm prefill path for DSA indexers under decode-context parallelism (`DCP > 1`).

The base ROCm DCP prefill (#65685) scores each rank's key shard and merges the per-rank top-k candidates. This adds a global-key path: all-gather every rank's FP8 index keys once per prefill chunk and take the top-k over the whole context, so no candidate merge is needed. On top of that, each rank can score `1/dcp` of the chunk's query rows and all-gather the selections once per layer.

items.author: mickqian
items.summary: Captures the FLUX.3 text encoder forward as a CUDA graph to eliminate ~35ms of host-side overhead per prompt in CFG parallel serving.
items.body:
## Motivation

The FLUX.3 text context is the eager `transformers` forward of a 32-layer language model over a prompt padded to a multiple of 80 tokens. On a B300 that is about 35 ms per prompt, and almost all of it is host time: the GPU work for a few hundred tokens is small, the Python forward that launches it is not. Under CFG parallel on two GPUs it is the largest part of a FLUX.3 request outside the denoising loop (text 0.036 s, decode 0.050 s, denoise 1.795 s).

Qwen-Image-2.1's stage already replays its text encoder's forward through CUDA graphs (`TextEncoderGraphs`) for the same reason

items.author: matthewygf
items.summary: On ROCm, a model that fuses RoPE with its KV write corrupts the unified KV arena's reserved padding slot. Slot 0 is the padding sink: graph padding rows write their dummy K and V there, and masked page-table entries read that page back.
items.body:
## Motivation

On ROCm, a model that fuses RoPE with its KV write corrupts the unified KV arena's reserved padding slot. Slot 0 is the padding sink: graph padding rows write their dummy K and V there, and masked page-table entries read that page back. The fused HIP writer stores to whatever destination it is handed, including slot 0, so the sink stops being zero. This PR skips the reserved destination and writes through the physical locations the attention backend already computed.

items.title: [Bugfix] Reject token-major layout for nvfp4 KV cache
items.author: nandanadileep
items.summary: Rejects token-major KV cache layouts for nvFP4 to prevent silent data corruption, since stride assumptions only hold for head-major page packing.
items.body:
## Problem

`--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4` silently corrupts the KV cache under a token-major layout (BLNHC/LBNHC). Fixes #61225.

The nvfp4 writer (`reshape_and_cache_nvfp4_dispatch`) derives data/scale strides for a side-contiguous `[data | scale]` page packing that only holds for head-major pages. Under a token-major layout it writes fp4 data and block scales to the wrong bytes, and the reader reads the garbage back — every K/V write (and its block scales) lands in the wrong location. No exception, no crash; just incoherent output at every context length.

## Description

This PR adds DeCo-Attention to VisualGen as an opt-in quantized-attention recipe of the `CUTEDSL` backend. The QK product of self-attention runs on NVFP4 operands, with the quantization error of the scores compensated inside the same matrix product; the PV product runs in FP8, or in NVFP4 on SM120. On Wan2.2 T2V at 720p the denoising is 1.68x faster than with BF16 attention on GB300, 1.73x on Rubin and 1.69x to 1.85x on RTX PRO 6000.

It is off by default and enabled per configuration:

```yaml
attention_config:
  backend: CUTEDSL
  quant_attention_config:
    qk_dtype: nvfp4

## Description

This PR lets git worktrees of TensorRT-LLM share one ccache. A fresh worktree then reuses the objects that another worktree already compiled, so its first build is much faster.

Before this PR, a fresh worktree missed ccache for every compile. ccache keys each object on its compile command, and that command holds the absolute paths of the source and build folders. A worktree at a new path therefore gets new keys. ccache's `base_dir` setting fixes this, but each user has to configure it. CI configures it in `jenkins/controlCCache.groovy`.

@coderabbitai summary

## Description

**Problem.** A `kv_cache_compression_config` method with a cold-page codec (today `quantization_for_cold_page`, NVFP4) makes `KVCacheManagerV2` encode pages when they leave the GPU for its host, disk or remote tiers. The `mooncake-store` connector takes the place of those tiers (it forces `host_cache_size` / `disk_cache_size` to 0 for roles that transfer KV), but it moved raw GPU pages, so with both configured the compression setting silently had no effect on the pool.

**Solution.** The connector now stores pages through the KV cache manager's own codec

## Description

The qwen4_exp cache manager keeps a QSA index-key plane next to the K/V pool. A page holds one row per token (`tokens_per_block`, 32): the token's raw index key, overwritten at the last token of each `compress_ratio` group by the group's compressed key. Index scoring reads only the compressed keys; a raw key is read once more, to pool its group, and is dead after that.

items.title: [Feature Request]Support FP32 bias gradient accumulation in native fused Linear backward
items.author: zjjott
items.summary: Accumulate bias gradients in FP32 instead of BF16 during fused Linear backward, reducing relative L2 error from ~1.67e-3 to ~6-8e-8.
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

When `gradient_accumulation_fusion=True`, native `LinearWithGradAccumulationAndAsyncCommunication` can accumulate weight gradients directly into FP32 `main_grad`, but its bias gradient still passes through BF16 before reaching the FP32 DDP buffer.

The relevant code is [`grad_bias = grad_output.sum(dim=0)` in layers.py](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/dev/megatron/core/tensor_parallel/layers.py#L962). With BF16 `grad_output`, this returns a BF16 result. Subsequent FP32 accumulation cannot recover the lost precision.

- At small batch with speculative decoding, Gemma4 decode is dominated by many small latency-bound ops between the FP8 GEMMs: norms, RoPE, FP8 casts, the per-layer-embedding tail and the assistant head.

The service still performs this setup only once, before inspecting its P2P queues. Transfer planning

### What does this PR do?

N-D data-parallel dispatch currently copies each shard to every rank in the model-parallel group. This adds an optional path that sends each data-parallel shard to exactly one model-parallel source rank and leaves redistribution to a worker-side preprocess hook. The worker does not create a model-parallel process group.

**Before:** `make_nd_compute_dataproto_dispatch_fn` always sent `arg[dp_rank]` to every worker on that data-parallel rank, and dispatch/collect metadata was a bare rank integer or bool.

**After:** Workers register `DispatchInfo(dp_rank, is_mp_src)`

items.summary: It adds, a KL penalty against the reference policy for. The estimator computes KL(πθ ‖ πref) exactly over the reference top-k tokens plus one tail bucket.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Implements the RFC in #8536. It adds `actor.kl_loss_type: topk_rb`, a KL penalty against the reference policy for `use_kl_loss=True`.

The estimator computes KL(π_θ ‖ π_ref) exactly over the reference top-k tokens plus one tail bucket. The within-tail part is estimated from the sampled token, so the result is an **unbiased** estimate of the full-vocabulary KL gradient at every k, with much lower variance than the single-sample `kl`/`k2`/`low_var_kl`/`k3+` options. It is the per-token Rao-Blackwellised KL of [Amini et al., NeurIPS 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.1063

### What does this PR do?

The torch backend of `FusedLinearForPPO` (the default fused backend) divides the bf16 logits by the temperature before upcasting to fp32, so log-probs differ from the rollout sampler’s formula (fp32 logits / T) by up to 0.054 at T=0.7, and the returned entropy is bf16. ## Summary

When context compaction splits an episode into multiple training rows, `rollout/raw_reward` gives that episode extra weight. For example, four episodes with rewards `[1, 0, 0, 0]` report a mean of `0.25`. Splitting the first and last episodes into two rows each raises the logged mean to `0.3333`, even though the episode rewards are identical.

Compute the mean over episodes before data-parallel partitioning. Each episode contributes equally, including when its segments land on different ranks. In the example above, the logged mean stays at `0.25` after splitting.

Preserve vLLM's `finish_reason="length"` in `TokenOutput.stop_reason`. Today the vLLM rollout server reports `completed` both when generation stops naturally and when the output budget cuts it off. goes to the server and refreshes the cached entry; where the directory is already visible it does nothing.

items.author: Aarav500
items.summary: In, call-based tests compared the generated function's return value with. The generated code controls that object, so a subclass of or whose always returns got full reward on every call-based task.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8656. In `prime_code`, call-based tests compared the generated function's return value with `output == expected`. The generated code controls that object, so a subclass of `int` or `list` whose `__eq__` always returns `True` got full reward on every call-based task. Swapping the operands doesn't help, because Python tries a subclass's reflected `__eq__` first.

This adds `_to_builtin()` in `prime_code/testing_util.py` and applies it to the output right after the existing `json.dumps(output)` call. It rebuilds the value from plain `None`/`bool`/`int`/`float

Enable a shared Mooncake KV cache pool for vLLM rollout, and turn on Ascend PD disaggregation on top of the existing GPU PD path.

Non-PD rollout attaches one Store connector (`MooncakeStoreConnector` on GPU, `AscendStoreConnector` on NPU). PD rollout keeps the P2P connector and wraps it with the Store connector in a `MultiConnector`.

items.body:
## Problem and behavior

Checkpoint participants each own one GPU, but Ray's default first barrier can enroll every visible GPU and its rendezvous key contains the local ordinal. The engine now owns a device-bound NCCLGroup specialization with a single-device barrier and a logical group key shared across masked/shared ordinal layouts. Allocation, executor-thread broadcast, synchronization and destruction use the engine device. Ordinary Ray groups retain their behavior, and duplicate ownership/topology checks remain. Delta transfers reuse this group and device without changing the wire protocol

items.title: Add `--logits-dtype` to keep Megatron actor logits in bf16
items.author: R0k1e
items.summary: upcasts the last pipeline stage's output to fp32 by default. slime calls the actor with, so the whole logits tensor is copied to fp32.
items.body:
## Motivation

`Float16Module.forward` upcasts the last pipeline stage's output to fp32 by default. slime calls the actor with `labels=None`, so the whole `[T, V]` logits tensor is copied to fp32. The LM head GEMM has already rounded these values to bf16, so the copy adds memory but no precision. It is the largest single allocation in a long-context actor step: 40,960 tokens × 248,320 vocabulary is about 41 GB in fp32 versus 20 GB in bf16.

The fp32 copy does one useful thing: every consumer of the logits computes in fp32 because its input is fp32. This PR keeps that guarantee, but enforces it

items.title: [fsdp] feat: project LM head only for response tokens
items.author: hxw12219
items.summary: Adds an opt-in FSDP engine option, (default ). RL losses read values only at response tokens, but the engine projects every packed token through the LM head.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds an opt-in FSDP engine option, `response_only_lm_head` (default `false`). RL losses read values only at response tokens, but the engine projects every packed token through the LM head. With the option on, the engine passes the packed rows that predict response tokens to the model as Transformers' `logits_to_keep`, so the eager and fused LM heads project only those rows. The values at response tokens are unchanged.

The saving grows with the prompt's share of each sequence: it is largest for long prompts with short responses and small for short prompts with long

## Summary

Fixes #2519.

`_apply_model_patch` chained `git apply --verbose`, `git apply --verbose --reject` and `patch --batch --fuzz=5 -p1 -i` with `||` and no reset in between. When the first `git apply` failed on one hunk, `--reject` applied the other hunks and exited non-zero. `patch --batch` then treated those hunks as a reversed patch, undid them, and could exit 0. The grader reported the patch as applied while the model's changes were gone, so a correct fix scored 0. The issue's standalone script reproduces this with GNU patch 2.8.1.

With `--sglang-speculative-algorithm DFLASH` and a colocated rollout engine, the first weight sync silently overwrites the DFLASH draft with target weights. After that, the acceptance length is ~1.0 and rollout is slower than with speculative decoding off.

items.title: fix(data): give uniform reward groups exactly zero advantage
items.author: saloni-garg
items.summary: When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about …
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In `_post_process_rewards` the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about an ulp instead of zero. With std normalization on, the residue is then divided by its own std, which turns it into a small nonzero advantage shared by the whole group.

Small reproduction on current main (a group of 16 rollouts that all scored 0.3, `grpo` with `grpo_std_normalization`):

-
discussion: The nonzero advantages for uniform fractional rewards reproduce on `main`. I ran the grouped-reward tests at `0063710` on CPU with PyTorch 2.13.0: uniform groups produce exact zeros, and the mixed-group and nonfinite-reward cases pass too.
Thank you for checking, and for reproducing it on main as well. Glad the tests hold up on your side too. Happy to run anything else you would like to see here.

items.author: Asthenia0412
items.summary: This coupled every submodule of (e.g.,, ) to the full async remote-reward runtime, even though most callers only need synchronous rule-based reward functions. [Discussion: Thanks for the review!]
items.body:
## Background

`vime.rollout.rm_hub.__init__` imported `aiohttp` at module load time. This
coupled every submodule of `rm_hub` (e.g. `math_utils`, `f1`, `gpqa`) to
the full async remote-reward runtime, even though most callers only need
synchronous rule-based reward functions.

## Problem

Running reward CPU tests in a lightweight contributor environment fails
during pytest collection, before any test body executes:

```
tests/test_rm_math.py:21: in <module>
    from vime.rollout.rm_hub.math_utils import (...)
vime/rollout/rm_hub/__init__.py:5: in <module>
    import aiohttp
E   ModuleNotFound

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.
items.body:
## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

items.title: fix(sglang): bound local server startup waits
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.
items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

## Background

When `group_rm` is enabled, the nested result was passed directly to the group reward function and trace helper. Those paths expect `list[Sample]`, so fan-out generation and group rewards could not be combined.

## Solution

## Solution

- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.

## Problem

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

Without `--offload-train`, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.

For one resumed run:

| | rollout logprob | reference logprob | actor logprob |

## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

## Description

items.body:
Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

items.body:
## Problem

Thanks to @kkyyxhll for catching in #2319 that SGLang ignores `sampling_params.temperature` when it computes input/prefill log-probs. OPD samples from the temperature-scaled student distribution `p_T`, so leaving the teacher at its implicit default computes `KL(p_T || q_1)`, not the matched-temperature objective `KL(p_T || q_T)`.

Passing the rollout temperature through sampling parameters is currently a no-op, while pinning it to `1.0` only makes the mismatched behavior explicit. Supporting the real-temperature case requires changing the SGLang input-logprob path.

items.title: [Rollout] Add vLLM encoder-prefill disaggregation
items.author: Gianthard-cyh
items.summary: This PR adds native vLLM Encoder-Prefill Disaggregation (EPD) to Vime. It uses and composes with the existing regular and PD rollout paths. [Discussion: <!-- readthedocs-1185709 --> ### Documentation build overview > 📚 📁 Comparing 20debb24fae27020e32403]
items.body:
This PR adds native vLLM Encoder-Prefill Disaggregation (EPD) to Vime. It uses `worker_type: encoder` and composes with the existing regular and PD rollout paths.

The implementation has two main parts:

1. Compile the user topology and group overrides into vLLM EC configuration during rollout-server orchestration.
2. Prime encoder engines from the rollout layer before the existing multimodal render/generate flow.

Related to #11.

## 1. Deployment configuration and override flow

The supported topologies are:
